text:
alex: repro'd a weird perf regression with stride-based KV prefetch + AWQ-int8 on a few Llama/Mistral configs. digging in, posting numbers and hypothesis.

jamie: summary pls — is this new or related to the earlier kv-warmup tweaks?

alex: new-ish — looks like an interaction between prefetch stride (we started testing stride:16) + RoPE scaling >1.0. when seq > 1024 we see throughput drop and a small but consistent accuracy delta on calibrated AWQ shards.

priya: can you drop the profiling run you used?

alex: sure, ran the harness on 1xA100, 48GB, model=llama-2-13b, quant=awq-int8, kernels=auto, prefetch=stride:16, seq=2048, batch=4. command:

```bash
./profile-run \
  --model llama-2-13b \
  --quant awq-int8 \
  --kernel auto \
  --kv-prefetch stride:16 \
  --seq 2048 \
  --batch 4 \
  --rope-scale 1.25
```

simple perf snip (mean of 5 runs):

perf_metric      | baseline (no-prefetch) | stride:16 enabled
-----------------|------------------------|------------------
tokens/sec       | 12.4k                 | 11.6k (-6.5%)
p95 latency (ms) | 210                   | 248 (+18%)
AWQ MRR (eval)   | 0.724                 | 0.712 (-1.7%)

matt: that MRR hit is small but consistent across seeds? might be noise.

alex: repeated 3 seeds, same direction. More interesting: kernel selector was switching to the "int8-block" matmul kernel at runtime for those batches. investigating L2/KV thrash. GPU profiler showed much higher L2 requests around KV gather stage.

eva: could RoPE scaling change memory layout so the strides interact badly with the matmul kernel tiling?

alex: exactly the hypothesis. when rope_scale != 1.0 the attention precompute path applies different rotary offsets, and our stride prefetcher issues load ranges that align poorly with the int8 kernel's preferred 128B coalescing. result: partial cache-line heavy loads, more L2 misses, and the int8 kernel's micro-tile suffers.

priya: do we see same on Mistral / Mixtral / Qwen?

alex: quick matrix: (A100 runs, same harness)
- mistral-7b + awq-int8: tokens/sec -3.2% with stride:16, p95 +10%
- mixtral-8x8 + awq-int8: negligible change (+0.5%)
- qwen-14b + gptq-int8: no regression (different kernel path)

jamie: so this looks model+kernel specific. any kernel fallback tests?

alex: tried forcing kernel=fp8-emulate (i know weird) and kernel=int8-alt. forcing fp8-emulate yields tokens/sec ~12.3k (near baseline) but AWQ calibration accuracy shifts a bit (calib interactions). forcing int8-alt (the other int8 matmul kernel) also restored throughput but had slightly higher MRR delta.

matt: can you paste the profiling flame around KV gather?

alex: pasted clipped nvprof text:

```
Time(%)  Kernel name                         Calls  Avg ms  GPU Mem Read  L2 Cache Load
28.1     int8_block_matmul                   120    3.2 ms   1.9GB         48M
12.4     kv_prefetch_stride                  240    1.1 ms   760MB         12M
7.8      attention_rope_apply                240    0.8 ms   120MB         3M
```

alex: note L2 cache load >> baseline case where int8_block_matmul was 18% time and L2 loads were ~30% lower.

eva: interesting. could we change stride param to 8 or adaptive to force alignment?

alex: tested stride:8 -> throughput -1.2%, p95 +4%. stride:auto (align to 128B boundaries) -> restores perf in 80% of cases.

priya: what about calibration prompts? AWQ calibrations sometimes change per-channel scales; could that influence which kernel is chosen?

alex: yes — calibration set matters. two calibration sets:
- calib-A (mix of short Q/A prompts) -> AWQ scales slightly larger variance -> favors int8_block_matmul choice
- calib-B (longer context, instruction-style) -> more conservative scales -> kernel selector picks int8-alt or fp8-emulate more often

perf/accuracy diff by calib set (llama-2-13b, stride:16):
- calib-A: tokens/sec 11.6k, MRR 0.712
- calib-B: tokens/sec 12.1k, MRR 0.718

jamie: uh. so calibration affects runtime kernel routing indirectly. sounds dangerous for stable SLAs.

alex: agreed. my working hypothesis: AWQ per-channel quant params change activation distribution such that our kernel-scorer picks int8_block when cost model thinks it's fastest, but with prefetch stride misalignment it's actually slower.

matt: mitigation ideas?

alex: shortlist:
1) kernel-selector change: add microbenchmark phase on first warmup batch to detect stride alignment penalty and pick alternate kernel (cheap runtime test).
2) adaptive prefetch: choose stride that aligns with chosen kernel's coalescing (align to 128B or 256B).
3) AWQ calibration profiling: attach a quick post-calib perf-check to bias selector away from int8_block if alignment penalty detected.
4) short-term: disable stride-prefetch for Llama-family with rope_scale !=1.0 by default.

priya: I like 1+2. cheap, localized, minimal accuracy risk.

eva: add test matrix for CI: all models x {stride:0,8,16,auto} x {rope_scale 1.0,1.25,0.8} x {awq,gptq}. we can run small microbench on PRs.

jamie: timeline?

alex: I'll prototype kernel-selector microbenchmark + adaptive prefetch in a branch this week. plan to roll a canary on dedicated infra next Tue.

infra-bot: deploy queued: branch/alex/kv-prefetch-adaptive ready for canary on infra-dedicated-03.

matt: assign followups: alex (implement), priya (CI matrix), eva (eval calibration sets), jamie (SLA impact note). cc eng-runtime. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — will post updates and the PR link here. if anyone wants the raw nvprof traces I uploaded them to s3: s3://redwood-internal/eng-runtime/profiles/1998877665/

priya: grabbing them now.

jamie: great thread, good catch.

alex: tagging for visibility @eng-runtime @eng-ml — this could explain some customer regressions reported last week.
